extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials, program managers, compliance officers, and legal counsel responsible for implementing Section 504 and agency accessibility/nondiscrimination obligations
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and standards that Executive agencies must follow to avoid discrimination on the basis of handicap, ensure program accessibility, communications, employment procedures, and complaints handling under Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Physical or mental impairment
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical or mental impairment includes any physiological disorder or condition, cosmetic disfigurement, or anatomical loss affecting body systems (neurological; musculoskeletal; special sense organs; respiratory, including speech organs; cardiovascular; reproductive; digestive; genitourinary; hemic and lymphatic; skin; and endocrine) or any mental or psychological disorder (e.g., mental retardation, organic brain syndrome, emotional or mental illness, specific learning disabilities). The term includes but is not limited to orthopedic, visual, speech, and hearing impairments, cerebral palsy, epilepsy, muscular dystrophy, multiple sclerosis, cancer, heart disease, diabetes, mental retardation, emotional illness, drug addiction and alcoholism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Major life activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Major life activities includes functions such as caring for one's self, performing manual tasks, walking, seeing, hearing, speaking, breathing, learning, and working.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Has a record of such an impairment
rubrics_metrics.description: Has a record of such an impairment means has a history of, or has been misclassified as having, a mental or physical impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Is regarded as having an impairment
rubrics_metrics.description: Is regarded as having an impairment means (i) has an impairment that does not substantially limit major life activities but is treated by the agency as constituting such a limitation; (ii) has an impairment that substantially limits major life activities only as a result of the attitudes of others toward such impairment; or (iii) has none of the impairments defined but is treated by the agency as having such an impairment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Handicapped person
rubrics_metrics.description: Handicapped person means any person who has a physical or mental impairment that substantially limits one or more major life activities, has a record of such an impairment, or is regarded as having such an impairment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Qualified handicapped person (program-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Qualified handicapped person means: (1) for preschool/elementary/secondary education, a handicapped person who is a member of a class otherwise entitled to receive education services; (2) for programs requiring performance or achievement, a handicapped person who meets essential eligibility requirements and can achieve the program purpose without modifications that would result in a fundamental alteration; (3) for other programs, a handicapped person who meets essential eligibility requirements for participation or receipt of benefits; (4) for employment, as defined in 29 CFR 1613.702(f) as made applicable by agency regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-evaluation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall, by August 24, 1987, evaluate current policies and practices and their effects that do not or may not meet the requirements of this part, and where modification is required shall proceed to make necessary modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must provide opportunity for interested persons (including handicapped persons or representative organizations) to participate via oral and written comments; keep on file for three years a description of areas examined and problems identified and a description of any modifications made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall make available to employees, applicants, participants, beneficiaries, and other interested persons information regarding the provisions of this part and its applicability to agency programs or activities, in such manner as the agency head finds necessary to apprise persons of protections against discrimination assured by Section 504 and the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: General prohibition: exclusion/denial of benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: No qualified handicapped person shall, on the basis of handicap, be excluded from participation in, be denied the benefits of, or otherwise be subjected to discrimination under any program or activity conducted by the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: deny opportunity to participate or benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may not, directly or through contractual, licensing, or other arrangements, deny a qualified handicapped person the opportunity to participate in or benefit from the aid, benefit, or service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: unequal opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may not afford a qualified handicapped person an opportunity to participate in or benefit from the aid, benefit, or service that is not equal to that afforded others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: ineffective aids, benefits, or services
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may not provide a qualified handicapped person with an aid, benefit, or service that is not as effective in affording equal opportunity to obtain the same result, gain the same benefit, or reach the same level of achievement as that provided to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: separate or different aids except when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may not provide different or separate aid, benefits, or services to handicapped persons or to any class of handicapped persons than is provided to others unless such action is necessary to provide qualified handicapped persons with aid, benefits, or services that are as effective as those provided to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: denial of participation on planning or advisory boards
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may not deny a qualified handicapped person the opportunity to participate as a member of planning or advisory boards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: limitation of rights, privileges, advantages, or opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may not otherwise limit a qualified handicapped person in the enjoyment of any right, privilege, advantage, or opportunity enjoyed by others receiving the aid, benefit, or service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition re: separate programs (non-separation defense not allowed)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may not deny a qualified handicapped person the opportunity to participate in programs or activities that are not separate or different, despite the existence of permissibly separate or different programs or activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition: administration criteria and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may not, directly or through other arrangements, utilize criteria or methods of administration the purpose or effect of which would (i) subject qualified handicapped persons to discrimination on the basis of handicap; or (ii) defeat or substantially impair accomplishment of the objectives of a program or activity with respect to handicapped persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site selection constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining the site or location of a facility, the agency may not make selections the purpose or effect of which would (i) exclude handicapped persons from, deny them the benefits of, or otherwise subject them to discrimination under any program or activity; or (ii) defeat or substantially impair the accomplishment of the objectives of a program or activity with respect to handicapped persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement contractor selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency, in the selection of procurement contractors, may not use criteria that subject qualified handicapped persons to discrimination on the basis of handicap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and certification administration
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may not administer a licensing or certification program in a manner that subjects qualified handicapped persons to discrimination on the basis of handicap, nor may the agency establish requirements for the programs or activities of licensees or certified entities that subject qualified handicapped persons to discrimination on the basis of handicap. However, programs or activities of licensees or certified entities are not themselves covered by this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most integrated setting
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall administer programs and activities in the most integrated setting appropriate to the needs of qualified handicapped persons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment nondiscrimination (application of Section 501/EEOC)
rubrics_metrics.description: No qualified handicapped person shall, on the basis of handicap, be subjected to discrimination in employment under any program or activity conducted by the agency. The definitions, requirements, and procedures of Section 501 of the Rehabilitation Act (29 U.S.C. 791), as established by the EEOC in 29 CFR part 1613, shall apply to employment in federally conducted programs or activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program accessibility for existing facilities (general obligation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall operate each program or activity so that the program or activity, when viewed in its entirety, is readily accessible to and usable by handicapped persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not necessarily require making each existing facility accessible; exceptions apply for historic preservation and where compliance would result in fundamental alteration or undue financial/administrative burdens (agency bears burden to prove and must issue written statement of reasons). When such exceptions apply the agency must take other actions that do not cause the alteration/burden but still ensure handicapped persons receive benefits and services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods to achieve program accessibility (existing facilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may comply through redesign of equipment, reassignment of services to accessible buildings, assignment of aides to beneficiaries, home visits, delivery at alternate accessible sites, alteration of existing facilities and construction of new facilities, use of accessible rolling stock, or any other methods that make programs readily accessible and usable by handicapped persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structural changes are not required where other methods are effective; in choosing methods, give priority to methods offering programs in the most integrated setting appropriate; when altering existing buildings meet accessibility requirements compelled by the Architectural Barriers Act and its implementing regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic preservation program exception & preferred methods
rubrics_metrics.description: In historic preservation programs, agencies need not take actions that would result in substantial impairment of significant historic features. In meeting program accessibility requirements, the agency shall give priority to methods that provide physical access to handicapped persons; where physical alteration is not required due to preservation constraints, alternative methods include using audio-visual materials to depict inaccessible portions, assigning persons to guide handicapped persons through portions that cannot otherwise be made accessible, or adopting other innovative methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance timeframes for existing facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall comply with obligations under program accessibility by October 21, 1986, except that where structural changes are undertaken such changes shall be made by August 22, 1989, but in any event as expeditiously as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition plan for structural changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If structural changes will be undertaken to achieve accessibility, the agency shall develop by February 23, 1987, a transition plan setting forth steps necessary to complete such changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency shall provide opportunity for interested persons (including handicapped persons or representative organizations) to participate by submitting oral and written comments; the transition plan must at minimum (1) identify physical obstacles limiting accessibility; (2) describe methods to make facilities accessible; (3) specify schedule and yearly steps if longer than one year; (4) indicate official responsible for implementation; and must be made available for public inspection.

rubrics_metrics.name: New construction and alterations accessibility standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Each building or part of a building constructed or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of the agency shall be designed, constructed, or altered to be readily accessible to and usable by handicapped persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions, requirements, and standards of the Architectural Barriers Act (42 U.S.C. 4151–4157) and implementing regulations (41 CFR 101–19.600 to 101–19.607) apply to buildings covered by this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications: obligation to ensure effective communication
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall take appropriate steps to ensure effective communication with applicants, participants, personnel of other Federal entities, and members of the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency shall furnish appropriate auxiliary aids where necessary to afford a handicapped person an equal opportunity to participate in and enjoy program benefits; in determining type of auxiliary aid give primary consideration to the handicapped person's requests; the agency need not provide individually prescribed devices, readers for personal use or study, or other devices of a personal nature; telephone communications with applicants and beneficiaries must use TDDs or equally effective telecommunication systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information and signage about accessible services
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall ensure that interested persons, including persons with impaired vision or hearing, can obtain information as to the existence and location of accessible services, activities, and facilities. The agency shall provide signage at a primary entrance to each inaccessible facility directing users to where they can obtain information about accessible facilities; the international symbol for accessibility shall be used at each primary entrance of an accessible facility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications fundamental alteration/undue burden exception and burden of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: The communications section does not require action that the agency can demonstrate would result in a fundamental alteration in the nature of a program or activity or in undue financial and administrative burdens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where agency personnel believe proposed action would fundamentally alter or cause undue burdens, agency has burden of proving compliance would result in such alteration or burdens; decision must be by agency head or designee after considering all resources and accompanied by written statement of reasons. If action would result in such alteration/burdens, agency shall take any other action that would not result in such alteration/burdens but would nevertheless ensure, to the maximum extent possible, that handicapped persons receive the benefits and services of the program or activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance procedures: jurisdiction and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The compliance procedures apply to all allegations of discrimination on the basis of handicap in programs or activities conducted by the agency, except that employment allegations are processed according to EEOC procedures under Section 501.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint filing and investigation timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall accept and investigate all complete complaints for which it has jurisdiction. All complete complaints must be filed within 180 days of the alleged act of discrimination; the agency may extend this time period for good cause. Within 180 days of receipt of a complete complaint for which it has jurisdiction the agency shall notify the complainant of the results of the investigation in a letter containing findings of fact and conclusions of law, a description of a remedy for each violation found, and a notice of the right to appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If agency lacks jurisdiction it shall promptly notify complainant and make reasonable efforts to refer complaint to the appropriate government entity; agency shall notify the Architectural and Transportation Barriers Compliance Board upon receipt of complaints alleging building/facility accessibility violations under the Architectural Barriers Act or Section 502 of the Rehabilitation Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal procedures and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals of findings of fact and conclusions of law or remedies must be filed by the complainant within 90 days of receipt from the agency of the investigation result letter. Timely appeals shall be accepted and processed by the head of the agency. The head shall notify the complainant of the results of the appeal within 60 days of receipt; if additional information is needed the head has 60 days from receipt of the additional information to make a determination. Time limits may be extended with permission of the Assistant Attorney General.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of investigative authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may delegate its authority for conducting complaint investigations to other Federal agencies, except that the authority for making the final determination may not be delegated to another agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Complete complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete complaint means a written statement that contains the complainant's name and address and describes the agency's alleged discriminatory action in sufficient detail to inform the agency of the nature and date of the alleged violation of Section 504. It shall be signed by the complainant or by someone authorized to do so on his or her behalf. Complaints filed on behalf of classes or third parties shall describe or identify (by name, if possible) the alleged victims of discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Auxiliary aids (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Auxiliary aids means services or devices that enable persons with impaired sensory, manual, or speaking skills to have an equal opportunity to participate in and enjoy the benefits of programs or activities. Examples for persons with impaired vision: readers, brailled materials, audio recordings, telecommunications devices. Examples for persons with impaired hearing: telephone handset amplifiers, telephones compatible with hearing aids, telecommunication devices for deaf persons (TDDs), interpreters, notetakers, written materials, and other similar services and devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Facility
rubrics_metrics.description: Facility means all or any portion of buildings, equipment, structures, roads, walks, parking lots, rolling stock or other conveyances, or other real or personal property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial impairment (historic preservation context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial impairment means a significant loss of the integrity of finished materials, design quality, or special character resulting from a permanent alteration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in assessing whether required accessibility actions would substantially impair significant historic features of a historic property (and thus allow alternative methods).
